source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: AA Col on athabasca
reports.comment: trip: The top layer of snow on the northwest face was completely wind loaded and could pose a risk for wind blown slabs

reports.title: Early Season Optimism
reports.comment: trip: With the weather station reading 16cm of fresh, this seemed like our best chance of getting some turns. The gully is still very rocky, the best skiing was actually below treeline, intersecting with the summer trail around 2050m. Lots of isolated reactive wind slabs in the alpine, shooting cracks. Didn't bother with a pit, average 15-20cm depth where it was actually skiable.

reports.title: Early Season Hilda Ridge
reports.comment: trip: 15 to 30cm of wind transported snow with very prominent surface hoar. A lot of facets, with wind crust in places. Other than the crown line on Mount Athabasca, no avalanche activity observed.

reports.title: Mt Athabasca avalanche
reports.comment: trip: Crown observed from the road.

reports.title: Wilcox Pass
reports.comment: trip: Skinned up to Wilcox Pass. From the parking lot to 2420m the snow varied from 5 to 20cm of facets with hoar on top, very variable due to wind transport, although no crust. Observed two avalanches and/or icefalls from Little Snow Dome onto the Athabasca Glacier.

reports.title: North Athabasca
reports.comment:
trip: Active snow transport with steady winds and cold temps. Well below ridgetop, mid slope bootpack tracks were filling in.
Saw recent natural small slide, see attached pic.
Varied surface conditions with wind effect.  At 3200m N asp, and 200m+ below ridgetop, we observed 15 to 30cm of 1F hard wind packed snow on top of softer snow. This surface was unsupportable punchy and boot pen was 70cm+. H…
